summary: Construct the commutative Q_l differential algebra encoding the l-adic homotopy type of a variety, through relative divided-power forms, finite-coefficient pro-simplicial systems and bidegreewise completion. Compare complex varieties with Sullivan rational minimal models, construct integer weight gradings from Frobenius, descend the complex grading to Q, and derive proper smooth formality and weight-bounded presentations for unipotent fundamental groups of normal varieties.

nodes.title: Strict graded commutativity on the existing DG carrier
nodes.statement: For a commutative coefficient ring R and an internally Z-graded R-algebra A with the existing TauCeti.IsDGAlgebra differential, impose A^p=0 for p<0, xy=(-1)^(pq)yx on homogeneous elements, and x²=0 for every homogeneous element of odd degree. This is extra structure on the existing carrier, not a replacement DG algebra. Over a characteristic-zero field the odd-square condition follows from the sign rule. Morphisms are existing DGAlgHom maps; quasi-isomorphism means isomorphism on every graded cohomology module. Connected means H⁰(A)=R when R is a field, not necessarily A⁰=R.
hypotheses: R is commutative; differential has degree +1; the underlying algebra need not be an ordinary commutative ring.

sources.match: The sign convention is used for the integral exterior-form construction.
Free graded-commutative algebras are the carriers of minimal models.

proofSteps: Refine the pinned internally graded algebra by homogeneous commutation and alternating odd generators. Use its cycles and boundaries quotient for cohomology.
Use DGAInfinity for the category, quasi-isomorphisms and localization; the new condition supplies the commutative subcategory.
acceptance: An exterior algebra on a degree-one module satisfies the integral condition.
An ordinary symmetric algebra with an odd generator over F₂ fails the odd-square condition even though its Koszul signs are trivial.

nodes.title: Polynomial homotopies of commutative DG maps
nodes.statement: For commutative DG algebras M,A over a characteristic-zero field K, a polynomial homotopy from f to g is a commutative DG map M→A⊗K[t,dt], where |t|=0, |dt|=1, d(t)=dt and (dt)²=0, whose evaluations at t=0 and t=1 give f and g. For a Sullivan source use the equivalence relation generated by such homotopies; prove that a single polynomial homotopy suffices and that composition descends. There is no division by factorials over arbitrary integral coefficients in this definition.
hypotheses: K is a characteristic-zero field.

nodes.title: Sullivan algebras and their minimal models
nodes.statement: A Sullivan algebra over K is a free graded-commutative algebra ΛV on positive-degree generators with a well-ordered exhaustive Hirsch-extension filtration such that the differential of each generator belongs to the preceding algebra. It is minimal if d(V) lies in the ideal of decomposables (Λ⁺V)². A minimal model of a connected nonnegative commutative DG algebra A is a quasi-isomorphism M→A from such a minimal algebra. A Hirsch extension by generators of degree r is A⊗ΛV with dV⊂A^(r+1), d²=0. A 1-minimal model uses only degree-one Hirsch extensions and has a map inducing an H¹ isomorphism and an H² injection; it is not generally a full quasi-isomorphism.
hypotheses: K is a characteristic-zero field; H⁰(A)=K.
Finite-dimensional H^i(A) does not assert finite-dimensional M^i or finitely many generators of each degree.

nodes.title: Existence, lifting and uniqueness of minimal models
nodes.statement: Every connected nonnegative commutative DG algebra over a characteristic-zero field has a Sullivan minimal model. A quasi-isomorphism A→B induces a bijection of homotopy classes of maps from any Sullivan algebra into A and B. A quasi-isomorphism between minimal Sullivan algebras is an isomorphism. Consequently two minimal models of A are isomorphic compatibly up to homotopy, and every automorphism of A lifts to an automorphism of a chosen minimal model up to homotopy. The isomorphism and the lifted automorphism are not unique as actual maps.
hypotheses: H⁰(A)=K; nonnegative degrees; K has characteristic zero.

sources.match: Degreewise Hirsch extensions kill obstructions and prove uniqueness in the homotopy category.
Provides the lifting mechanism; Morgan supplies the general connected full-model statement beyond the simply connected case treated first here.

proofSteps: Adjoin closed generators to make H^r surjective and generators of degree r−1 to kill its kernel, allowing repeated extensions in degree one.
Use the relative obstruction Hom(V,H^(r+1)(cone(f))) for each Hirsch extension. It vanishes for a quasi-isomorphism.
Apply lifting in both directions and minimality to obtain an isomorphism. Lift the inverse automorphism as well; minimal rigidity makes the representative invertible.
acceptance: Do not replace the connected hypothesis by simple connectivity.
Nonunique automorphisms inducing the same cohomology map are allowed.

nodes.title: The rank-one divided-power coordinate
nodes.statement: Identify the existing divided-power algebra Γ_Z(Z) with the subring of Q[t] consisting of finite sums Σ a_n t^n/n! with a_n∈Z. Write γ_n=t^n/n!, put γ_n in t-degree n and define R{t}=R⊗_Z Z{t}. The presentation has γ_0=1 and γ_mγ_n=binom(m+n,m)γ_(m+n); it is free as a Z-module on the γ_n. For a Q-algebra it identifies with R[t], but the basis normalization is retained for integral and finite coefficients.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; finite sums are used.

sources.match: Specifies the concrete coordinate algebra and grading; the universal divided-power algebra is supplied by Mathlib.

proofSteps: Send the universal γ_n(1) to t^n/n! and prove the defining relations by binomial identities.

Establish the rank-one free basis and injectivity into Q[t], then scalar extend this presentation. Mathlib supplies the quotient construction and product relation, not the unverified basis comparison.
acceptance: Multiplication by t sends γ_n to (n+1)γ_(n+1).
The integral construction does not invert factorials in R.

nodes.title: The t-grading of relative forms
nodes.statement: A t-graded commutative DG R{t}-algebra is a direct sum of modules Ω_n^p for p,n≥0, with differential Ω_n^p→Ω_n^(p+1), product Ω_n^p×Ω_m^q→Ω_(n+m)^(p+q), and γ_r of bidegree (0,r). Its total cochain degree is p. In the simplex-form objects require Ω_n^p=0 for p>n. The t-grading is distinct from the weight grading introduced on characteristic-zero minimal models.
hypotheses: R is commutative; exterior degree is p and t-degree is n.

sources.match: The two gradings have different differentials and degree bounds.

proofSteps: Use direct sums of the existing modules and graded algebra carrier. Differential raises p and fixes n.
Define bidegreewise morphisms and limits before forming total direct sums; inverse limits do not create a completed product over t-degrees.
acceptance: d preserves n even though it raises p.
t-degree support of every element is finite in the total direct sum.

nodes.title: Relative divided-power forms on a simplex
nodes.statement: For a finite nonempty set σ put L=R^σ and Q=L/R·(1,…,1). Define Ω(σ,R)=Γ_R(L)⊗_RΛ_R(Q). Its differential is the divided-power derivation dγ_r(x)=γ_(r−1)(x)·bar(x), extended by d(bar(x))=0 and the graded Leibniz rule. Give γ_r(x) t-degree r and bar(x) t-degree 1. Equivalently take divided-power polynomial forms on coordinates x_i and quotient by the differential ideal generated by dt=Σdx_i, where t=Σx_i. Do not quotient by t−1. Scalar extension is applied to simplex coefficients before any simplicial mapping object.
hypotheses: σ is finite and nonempty; R is a commutative ring.
The quotient L/R·diag is free, because one coordinate splits the diagonal inclusion.

sources.match: The intrinsic divided-power tensor exterior construction gives the relative forms and their coefficient extension.

proofSteps: Use the existing divided-power and exterior algebra universal properties to define the derivation and the tensor product.
Check the divided-power relations, d²=0 and the quotient by dt. Identify the integral construction followed by tensoring with the intrinsic R-construction.
A monomial of exterior degree p has at least t-degree p; this proves the triangular support.
acceptance: For one vertex Ω(σ,R)=R{t} in cochain degree zero, not R.

nodes.title: Pullback of relative forms
nodes.statement: For every map of finite nonempty sets φ:τ→σ there is a t-graded commutative DG pullback φ*:Ω(σ,R)→Ω(τ,R), sending x_i to Σ_(φ(j)=i)x_j and dx_i to the corresponding sum of dx_j. These maps preserve t, commute with coefficient change, and satisfy identity and contravariant composition laws. Restriction to ordinal maps gives a simplicial algebra, including all degeneracies.
hypotheses: Finite nonempty σ,τ; no injectivity or surjectivity hypothesis on φ.

sources.match: The finite-set functor gives faces and degeneracies of the coefficient object.

proofSteps: Pull back the coordinate module by summing over fibres and observe that the diagonal vector maps to the diagonal vector.
Apply functoriality of Γ and Λ and check d on divided-power generators. Use the divided-power addition identity for a noninjective φ.
acceptance: A face map sets omitted coordinates and their differentials to zero.
For the collapse {0,1}→{0}, γ₂(x₀) pulls back to γ₂(x₀)+x₀x₁+γ₂(x₁), not just the sum of its two pure terms.

nodes.title: Divided-power forms on a simplicial set
nodes.statement: For a simplicial set X define Ω_n^p(X,R)=Hom_sSet(X,UΩ_n^p(−,R)), where U forgets the module structure of the simplicial coefficient object. The group and R-module structures are pointwise. Put Ω(X,R)=⊕_(p,n)Ω_n^p(X,R), with pointwise product and differential. This is contravariant in X and covariant in R, with 0≤p≤n support. A family must respect faces and degeneracies. Tensor coefficients into each simplex-form module first: Ω(X,Z)⊗R is not used as the definition of Ω(X,R).
hypotheses: X is any simplicial set; R is a commutative ring.

sources.match: Compatible families supply the mapping definition and its two variance directions.

proofSteps: Form the simplicial coefficient modules from simplex pullback, then the sets of simplicial maps into their underlying sets.
Pointwise operations give modules and the product. Sum over bidegrees to retain finite t-support rather than silently taking a product.
acceptance: Restriction to a representable simplex recovers its coefficient algebra by Yoneda.
For a simplicial complex the result is the compatible-family construction; the geometric cone is motivation and requires no extra carrier.

nodes.title: Homotopy of the simplicial coefficient modules
nodes.statement: For p,n,i≥0, the homology in degree i of the normalized chain complex of the simplicial R-module Ω_n^p(−,R) is R if i=p=n and is zero otherwise. The identification in the exceptional degree is natural in R. Here homology refers to the simplicial direction, not the cochain differential d of forms. This calculation is the coefficient resolution input to the integral cohomology comparison.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring.

sources.match: The source reduces the coefficient homotopy to the diagonal quotient and a décalage calculation, without giving its full proof.

proofSteps: Normalize σ↦R^σ; its chain complex is R→R with identity differential in degrees 1 and 0, hence contractible.
Use an explicit simplicial contraction on its divided-power algebra. An arbitrary nonlinear functor preserving chain homotopy is not a sufficient substitute.
The diagonal quotient is K(R,1); establish the exterior-power décalage calculation for this free rank-one object and combine the t-degrees. Gap G1 records the unread décalage and extension proof.
acceptance: For p=n=0 the simplicial coefficient module is constant R with H₀=R.
For (p,n)=(0,1) normalization is acyclic; for (1,1) it has H₁=R.

nodes.title: The triangular integral cohomology comparison
nodes.statement: For every simplicial set X and commutative ring R there is a natural multiplicative isomorphism H^p(Ω_n(X,R))≃H^p(X,R)·γ_n for n≥p, and H^p(Ω_n(X,R))=0 for n<p. Together these identify H*Ω with the triangular subalgebra ⊕_(0≤p≤n)H^p(X,R)γ_n of H*(X,R)⊗R{t}. Under it the product of classes aγ_n and bγ_m is binom(n+m,n)(a∪b)γ_(n+m). The target is ordinary simplicial cohomology with its cup product, not homotopy groups or the full untapered tensor algebra.
hypotheses: X is arbitrary; no finite-dimensionality assumption.

sources.match: States the coefficient-natural ring comparison and points to Miller for the cohomology proof.

proofSteps: Use the normalized simplicial coefficient calculation to construct the natural cohomology comparison and prove its additive isomorphism.
Establish the extension/acyclicity argument for compatible forms on successive skeleta, including passage to an infinite simplicial set; G1 identifies the missing proof reference.
Check cup-product compatibility on universal simplicial cocycles, tracking the divided-power binomial coefficient. Import ordinary cohomology from AlgebraicTopology stage 6.
acceptance: For the simplicial circle H¹Ω_n≃R for n≥1 and H¹Ω₀=0.
For a two-torus, multiplying two independent degree-one classes in t-degree 1 gives 2(a∪b)γ₂; reduction mod 2 makes this product zero although H²(X,F₂) is nonzero.

nodes.title: Quotient coefficients and the exceptional diagonal
nodes.statement: For a principal ideal quotient B=R/(a) of a commutative ring, the natural map Ω_n^p(X,R)⊗_R B→Ω_n^p(X,B) is an isomorphism for n≠p. In the exceptional diagonal the complex has a right-exact sequence Ω_p^(p−1)(X,R)→Ω_p^p(X,R)→H^p(X,R)→0, natural in coefficients. In particular the coefficient transition maps at fixed (p,n), n≠p, are surjective. Do not assert the global base-change isomorphism on n=p or for arbitrary quotient ideals on infinite X: E10 gives a counterexample to the unrestricted printed assertion.
hypotheses: X is a simplicial set; p,n≥0; B=R/(a), including Z→Z/l^r and Z/l^(r+1)→Z/l^r.

sources.match: The off-diagonal assertion supplies the principal-quotient input to completion; E10 corrects its unrestricted ring generality.

proofSteps: Prove the principal-quotient assertion from the extendable coefficient resolution; G1 includes this proof. Keep coefficient products explicit: tensoring by an arbitrary quotient need not commute with them.

nodes.statement: For a characteristic-zero field K define A_PL(Δ^r;K) as K[x₀,…,x_r,dx₀,…,dx_r]/(Σx_i−1,Σdx_i), with polynomial degree-zero coordinates, exterior degree-one differentials and d(x_i)=dx_i. Put A_PL(X;K)=Hom_sSet(X,A_PL(Δ^•;K)), interpreted degree by degree. It is a commutative DG algebra. The polynomial degree filtration counts both x_i and dx_i; on a general infinite X this means a uniform bound on every simplex when the bound is imposed.
hypotheses: K has characteristic zero; X is a simplicial set.

sources.match: Polynomial compatible forms and their rational de Rham theorem.
The rational polynomial-form algebra provides the topological model used by minimal algebras.
Barycentric polynomial degree describes the comparison with relative forms.

nodes.statement: There is a natural t-graded DG injection Ω(X,K)→A_PL(X;K)⊗K[t], sending x_i to t·x_i and dx_i to t·dx_i. Its t-degree n image is t^n times the forms whose total barycentric polynomial degree is at most n. Multiplication by t induces a natural quasi-isomorphism colim_n Ω_n(X,K)→A_PL(X;K). The first map is not generally an isomorphism of the whole graded algebras. The stabilized map need not be surjective as an actual map of form sets for an infinite X with unbounded simplexwise polynomial degrees.

nodes.title: The mod-l finiteness condition
nodes.statement: The condition (F) on a pro-simplicial set at the prime l says that H^i(X,Z/l) is finite for every i≥0. It is degreewise finiteness and does not require a uniform bound on the number of nonzero degrees. Define H^i(X,Z_l)=lim_r H^i(X,Z/l^r) as a Z_l-module, and H^i(X,Q_l)=H^i(X,Z_l)⊗_(Z_l)Q_l. These names alone do not assert finite generation or an interchange of inverse limit and cohomology.

sources.match: Degreewise mod-l finiteness controls the inverse system and rational coefficients.

nodes.statement: Under (F), each H^i(X,Z/l^r) is finite, H^i(X,Z_l) is a finitely generated Z_l-module, and for every r≥1 there is a natural short exact sequence 0→H^i(X,Z_l)⊗Z/l^r→H^i(X,Z/l^r)→Tor₁^(Z_l)(H^(i+1)(X,Z_l),Z/l^r)→0. In particular H^i(X,Q_l) is finite-dimensional. Torsion in H^(i+1) cannot be dropped from the formula.

sources.match: Cites SGA5 V 5.3.1 for the finite-generation and universal-coefficient argument.

The mod-l bound is degreewise; no bounded total cochain complex is assumed.

nodes.title: Bidegreewise completion and its cohomology
nodes.statement: For a pro-simplicial set satisfying (F), define Ω_n^p(X,Z_l)=lim_r Ω_n^p(X,Z/l^r), and then take the direct sum over (p,n) to get a t-graded commutative DG Z_l{t}-algebra. Its cohomology in t-degree n is H^p(X,Z_l)γ_n for p≤n and zero for p>n. The inverse-limit statement includes proof of exactness on the cycles and boundaries systems; finite cohomology alone is not permission to commute arbitrary limits.
hypotheses: The mod-l finiteness condition (F) holds; inverse limits are taken before total direct sums.

sources.match: Uses off-diagonal surjectivity and the diagonal cohomology cokernel to justify completion.

proofSteps: Off the diagonal the quotient-coefficient theorem makes the module transitions surjective.

On n=p use the natural right-exact sequence from Ω_p^(p−1) to Ω_p^p to finite H^p; the boundary images are ML and the finite quotient is ML. Verify the module, cycle and boundary systems needed for the inverse-limit exactness theorem.
Apply the countable ML exactness criterion to identify completed cohomology. G2 includes this criterion and its application, beyond the pinned ML predicate.
acceptance: Completion does not introduce an infinite sum over t-degrees.
The diagonal argument must use finite cohomology; off-diagonal surjectivity is not a proof on the diagonal.

nodes.title: Étale realization of the homotopy algebra
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type k-scheme X over an algebraically closed field, with l invertible in k, choose a countable algebraically closed field of definition k₁⊂k and a model X₁. Choose a cofinal étale hypercovering system of X₁, apply connected components degreewise, and obtain a pro-simplicial set Et(X₁). Set A_l(X)=A_l(Et(X₁)). Étale hypercover descent, algebraically closed base extension and finite-coefficient finiteness give (F) and H* A_l(X)≃H*_(ét)(X,Q_l) as rings. Different choices are linked by quasi-isomorphisms through common refinements; the result is a contravariant functor in the category obtained by inverting quasi-isomorphisms, not a literal choice-free algebra.
hypotheses: X is separated and of finite type over algebraically closed k; l≠char(k).
Apply connected minimal models separately to connected components.

nodes.title: Galois action and its finite-level continuity
nodes.statement: If X descends to a variety X₀ over a countable field k₀ and k₁ is its algebraic closure in k, a Galois-stable covering system gives an action of Gal(k₁/k₀) on the constructed A_l(X), inducing the usual Galois action on H*_(ét)(X,Q_l). At every fixed r the action on Ω(Et(X₁),Z/l^r), with the discrete topology, is continuous: each form has open stabilizer. No topology on the full minimal model, continuity in a proalgebraic automorphism group, or continuous lifting to an actual minimal-model action is concluded.
hypotheses: k₀ is countable; X₀ is separated finite type; l invertible in k₀.

sources.match: Galois acts through the construction, while continuity is asserted only on finite-coefficient forms.

proofSteps: Choose a system stable under Galois, retaining descent data at each finite stage.

Prove finite-level open stabilizers using a finite-skeleton bound for each fixed (p,n) coefficient module, then a finite field extension defining the finitely many covering components and form data. A form is not presumed to have finite data merely because it belongs to a mapping object; this finite-width point is part of G1. Transport the action through the coefficient and t limits as algebraic maps.

nodes.title: Good-cover refinement of complex étale systems
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type complex variety X and a countable étale covering system of a countable field-of-definition model, construct a cofinal compatible system of analytic open covers of X(C), refining the analytifications of the étale maps, such that every nonempty finite intersection is contractible. The nerves N_α have the homotopy type of X(C) and define a morphism of pro-simplicial systems N→Et(X₁). The resulting map on cohomology with Z/l^r coefficients is the étale–analytic comparison. Finite CW type is used for finite-generation comparisons; one must not assume an arbitrary noncompact analytic good cover is finite.
hypotheses: Complex algebraic X, separated finite type; l prime, r≥1.

sources.match: Constructs nerves with contractible intersections and a comparison of systems, invoking SGA4 XVI 4.1.

proofSteps: Use triangulability/local contractibility and a compatible good-cover refinement to lift analytic opens through étale local homeomorphisms. Gap G3 names the good-cover and finite-CW inputs not supplied by the current RealAlgebraicGeometry roadmap.
Use the nerve theorem and the SF.2 étale–analytic comparison to identify cohomology.
Keep refinement choices in the pro-system so maps between different choices are compared by common refinements.
acceptance: A noncompact open curve is permitted; compactness is not a hidden hypothesis.
An arbitrary cover with a noncontractible intersection is insufficient to invoke the nerve theorem.

nodes.title: Complex comparison of minimal models
nodes.statement: Let X be a connected separated finite-type complex variety and M_Q→A_PL(X(C);Q) a Sullivan minimal model, using a simplicial model of X(C). There is a zigzag of quasi-isomorphisms of commutative DG Q_l-algebras from A_l(X) to A_PL(X(C);Q)⊗Q_l, inducing the usual cohomology comparison. Consequently M_Q⊗Q_l is a minimal model of A_l(X), and any chosen minimal model of A_l(X) is isomorphic to it, compatibly with a natural homotopy class of comparisons. The resulting actual algebra isomorphism need not be canonical.
hypotheses: X is connected; l prime; étale–analytic comparison and finite CW type are available.

sources.match: The finite-coefficient comparison passes through completion and rational stabilization before taking minimal models.

proofSteps: Use Ω(Et(X₁),Z/l^r)→Ω(N,Z/l^r) and a chosen nerve stage to obtain bidegree quasi-isomorphisms.
Apply the proved ML comparison to pass to Z_l, then rationalize and stabilize in t. Justify the integral-to-Z_l cohomology comparison by finite CW type, not by an unrestricted tensor/Hom identity.
Compare the rational stabilized nerve algebra to A_PL and pass to minimal models by EH.0.
acceptance: For X=G_m,C the model is Λ(a₁)⊗Q_l, with one H¹ class.
For a complex elliptic curve the model is Λ(a₁,b₁)⊗Q_l; its two H¹ generators multiply to the H² generator.

nodes.title: Geometric cohomology weight filtrations
nodes.statement: For a separated finite-type complex variety X, take the geometric mixed Hodge structure on H^i(X(C),Q) and its increasing weight filtration W. For a separated finite-type variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from l, take the cohomological weight filtration furnished by a suitable spread and its mixed cohomology realization. The comparison needed here has finite exhaustive W, is functorial, and makes cup product and Künneth maps filtered. In degree i the weights lie in [0,2i]; if X is smooth they lie in [i,2i], if X is proper in [0,i], and if X is normal H¹ has weights in [1,2]. In the complex case the normal-crossing hyperresolution weight construction gives exactly the W of the geometric mixed Hodge structure, not an arbitrary filtration on its underlying vector space.
hypotheses: X separated finite type; l invertible for the étale realization.
Geometric mixed Hodge realization and spread-independent weight comparison are the inputs isolated in G4; the pinned abstract MixedHodgeStructure carrier alone does not construct them.

sources.match: Proper normal-crossing hyperresolutions construct geometric mixed Hodge cohomology, its independence and its products.
Normality controls H¹ and arithmetic weights recover the geometric Hodge weight filtration.

proofSteps: Use SF.4 resolution and compactification to obtain a proper hyperresolution with smooth proper compactifications and SNC boundaries; import the log de Rham sheaf from ComplexComparisonPartII.

The missing geometric Hodge input consists of a rational/complex mixed Hodge complex with the comparison, strictness and descent required by Hodge III 8.1.19–20. Its complex filtration index shifts on H^i: W_m H^i is induced from W_(m−i) on the weight complex.

Use smooth proper strata and Tate twists in the weight spectral sequence to identify both realizations and the stated bounds. For normal H¹ use the stronger normal-variety result of Poids 8.3. G4 and the HodgeStructures Part III ownership proposal keep this input explicit.
acceptance: For G_m, H¹ has weight 2; for an elliptic curve, H¹ has weight 1.
A proper singular variety need not have pure cohomology; the nodal rational curve has weight-0 H¹, so the normality hypothesis in the H¹ bound is essential.

nodes.title: Geometric Frobenius splitting of Hodge weights
nodes.statement: Let X be a complex variety defined over k₀ finitely generated over Q, and choose an integral finite-type Z-model with l inverted. After shrinking that model there are good closed points s with residue cardinality q>1 and geometric Frobenius lifts σ such that the eigenvalues of σ on H^i(X(C),Q)⊗Q_l are algebraic Weil q-numbers. The sum of their generalized eigenspaces of weights at most m is W_m H^i(X(C),Q)⊗Q_l. Thus the Weil weight homomorphism used on the minimal model splits the scalar extension of the geometric Hodge weight filtration. The splitting depends on σ; the cohomological filtration does not.
hypotheses: Finite-type separated complex X; k₀ finitely generated; l invertible on the spread; geometric, not arithmetic, Frobenius.

sources.match: A spread with good closed fibers identifies Frobenius weight subspaces with the Hodge weight filtration.
Applies this cohomology comparison to an automorphism of the Q_l minimal model.

proofSteps: Spread a common normal-crossing hyperresolution and all comparison maps over an open of a finitely generated integral Z-algebra.
Apply the DWP.7 purity theorem to smooth proper strata and track all Tate twists in the weight spectral sequence.
Strictness and degeneration identify the resulting weight filtration on Betti and étale cohomology. Generalized eigenspaces distinguish weights even when Frobenius has nontrivial Jordan blocks.
acceptance: For geometric Frobenius on H²(P¹), eigenvalue q has weight 2, fixing the dual/Tate convention.
The opposite Frobenius convention gives q^(−1), which would have weight −2 and contradict the intended comparison.

nodes.title: Exhaustive finite-type filtrations of minimal models
nodes.statement: An admissible filtration of a Sullivan minimal algebra M is an increasing sequence M₀⊂M₁⊂… of differential graded subalgebras, each generated by finitely many positive-degree elements, whose union is M. Stability under an automorphism means that it carries each M_n onto itself, not merely into it. Every cochain degree of each M_n is finite-dimensional, but a cochain degree of the union M may be infinite-dimensional. An automorphism preserving this filtration is locally finite on every degree of M.
hypotheses: K is characteristic zero; M is a connected Sullivan minimal algebra with finite-dimensional H^i(M) for each i when existence is invoked.

sources.match: Finite-type subalgebras make the generalized eigenvalue construction possible.

proofSteps: Represent subalgebras with inherited grading and differential; record finite positive generator sets and exhaustivity.
For a fixed degree, finitely many positive-degree generators allow finitely many monomials, proving local finite-dimensionality and then local finiteness for stable automorphisms.
acceptance: A degree truncation of M is generally not a subalgebra.
A finite collection of generators without their differential dependencies need not generate a DG subalgebra.

Filtered automorphism groups are expressed as an inverse system of algebraic groups.

nodes.title: Stable representatives of homotopy automorphisms
nodes.statement: For a connected nonnegative commutative DG algebra A over a characteristic-zero field, with each H^i(A) finite-dimensional, a chosen minimal model M admits an admissible finite-type filtration such that every automorphism of M is homotopic to an automorphism preserving that filtration. In particular an automorphism of A can be lifted, up to homotopy, to a filtration-preserving automorphism of M. This assertion does not say that the original automorphism preserves the chosen filtration.
hypotheses: H⁰(A)=K; every H^i(A) finite-dimensional; K characteristic zero.

sources.match: Asserts the admissible-filtration property from the inductive construction of a minimal model.
The canonical Hirsch-extension filtration explains the induction and the degree-one finiteness caveat.

proofSteps: Construct a countable sequence of finite Hirsch-extension blocks, closing each block under the finitely many differential dependencies.
Use the homotopy lifting/obstruction calculation to replace an arbitrary automorphism by one adapted to those blocks.

For degree-one extensions and higher degrees verify that finite cohomology is sufficient for the finite-block choices. G5 records this technical filtration argument and the common-filtration refinement; finite-dimensionality of M^i is not an assumption.
acceptance: For a simply connected finite-type model the familiar degree filtration can be refined by finite generator blocks.
The connected case with nonnilpotent π₁ is retained, so a proof restricted to finite generator spaces per degree is insufficient.

nodes.title: Multiplicative generalized eigenvalue grading
nodes.statement: Let σ be an automorphism of a minimal commutative DG K-algebra M preserving an admissible finite-type filtration. Over an algebraic closure Kbar set M(a)=union_(r≥1)ker((σ−a)^r) for a∈Kbar×, degreewise in M⊗Kbar. Then M⊗Kbar=⊕_a M(a), d preserves a, and M(a)M(b)⊂M(ab). These are generalized eigenspaces for a locally finite automorphism; neither semisimplicity nor finite-dimensionality of the whole degree of M is required.
hypotheses: K characteristic zero; σ is invertible and preserves an admissible filtration.

sources.match: Defines the generalized-eigenvalue grading and its multiplicative type.

proofSteps: Restrict to finite-dimensional graded pieces of M_n and use primary decomposition over a splitting field.
Show independence under inclusion of the finite pieces and take their union.
For x,y in generalized eigenspaces use the tensor product spectrum to obtain the ab generalized eigenspace for xy. Commutation with d preserves the eigenvalue.
acceptance: A Jordan block belongs to one generalized eigenspace; ordinary eigenspaces alone fail to span.
The eigenvalue indexing set is multiplicative, so multiplication sends (a,b) to ab rather than a+b.

nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a minimal model come from cohomology
nodes.statement: For M,σ as in the generalized-eigenvalue construction, every eigenvalue a on M^n⊗Kbar is a finite product ∏α_j of eigenvalues α_j on positive-degree cohomology H^(r_j)(M)⊗Kbar, with Σr_j≥n. The unit in degree zero uses the empty product. The inequality is in this direction because a generator that kills a cohomology relation in degree r may have degree r−1. Eigenvalues may be taken from the spherical cohomology quotients appearing in the Hirsch-extension induction.
hypotheses: M is a connected Sullivan minimal model with finite-dimensional cohomology; σ respects an admissible filtration.

sources.match: The product assertion, including the degree inequality, is the mechanism for model weight bounds.

proofSteps: Induct along minimal Hirsch extensions: closed generators obtain eigenvalues from new cohomology; generators killing relations obtain eigenvalues from decomposable cocycles in the preceding algebra.
Multiplicativity propagates product expressions to monomials. The differential raises degree without changing eigenvalue, giving Σr_j≥n.
For possibly infinite degree-one towers make the induction compatible with the finite blocks of G5.
acceptance: In the even-sphere model with σx=ax and dy=x², σy=a²y: its source cohomology degree sum is 4≥3.
No eigenvalue is allowed to arise from arbitrary extra contractible generator pairs, which minimality excludes.

nodes.title: Integer weight gradings and their lower bounds
nodes.statement: Let Γ⊂Kbar× contain all eigenvalues of σ on M and let v:Γ→Z be a group homomorphism. Coarsen the eigenvalue grading by M_w=⊕_(v(a)=w)M(a). This is a Z-weight grading with d of weight 0 and multiplicative weights. If v(α)≥0 on every positive-degree cohomology eigenvalue, all model weights are nonnegative. If v(α)≥i for eigenvalues on H^i, then M^n has only weights w≥n. If v extends to a Galois-invariant homomorphism on a Galois-stable subgroup, the grading descends to K. For K=Q_l and q>1 a prime power, use the all-complex-embeddings Weil q-weight homomorphism on algebraic numbers, imported from DWP.0.
hypotheses: σ is a filtration-preserving automorphism; v is defined on a group containing its spectrum.
Descent requires the stated Galois invariance; choosing one complex embedding is insufficient.

sources.match: Coarsening gives integer model weights, the two lower bounds, and descent.

proofSteps: Sum generalized eigenspaces over equal values of v; directness follows from primary decomposition.
Apply the eigenvalue-product theorem to prove both bounds.
Galois invariance makes each weight subspace invariant under coefficient-field descent; descend the finite invariant pieces and take their union.
acceptance: For an even-sphere model with weight(x₂)=2 and dy=x², weight(y₃)=4, so the differential preserves weight and model weight may exceed degree.
Weight bounds on cohomology do not imply semisimplicity of σ.

nodes.title: A common filtration for finitely many automorphisms
nodes.statement: For the minimal algebra M of a connected finite-cohomology commutative DG algebra over a characteristic-zero field, every finite set of actual automorphisms of M admits a single admissible finite-type filtration stable under each of them. The automorphisms are not required to generate a finite group. For two algebraic weight G_m-actions, choose such a filtration for their values at a scalar such as 2; local finiteness and Zariski density of its powers then show that the same filtration is graded for both actions.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero; finite-dimensional H^i(M); finitely many automorphisms, not a finite generated group assumed finite.

sources.match: The lemma is stated without proof and is required to extend filtered conjugacy to arbitrary weight gradings.

proofSteps: Construct finite generator blocks closed under d and the indicated maps and their inverses, using minimal-extension obstructions to prevent an uncontrolled infinite orbit closure.
Prove finite generation of each block and exhaustivity simultaneously; taking all iterates of a finite set without proving finite-dimensional span does not suffice.

For a rational torus action each element has finite weight support; a finite-dimensional subspace invariant under the operator 2^w and its inverse is a sum of its weight spaces. G5 records the missing full proof of the block-construction lemma.
acceptance: Two commuting or noncommuting automorphisms are allowed; averaging over a finite group is not a proof.
A proof only after replacing the automorphisms by homotopic representatives does not prove this assertion about the original two gradings.

nodes.title: Filtered automorphism schemes and the weight extension
nodes.statement: Fix an admissible filtration of M over a characteristic-zero field K. Let G₁ be the inverse limit of the affine algebraic groups of DG automorphisms of M_n preserving all earlier M_j. Use restrictions and their scheme-theoretic images when needed. For a multiplicative cohomology filtration W finite on each H^i define G₂⊂G₁×G_m by pairs (g,λ) preserving W and acting as λ^w on Gr_w^W H*(M). Write U=ker(G₂→G_m). An algebraic section of G₂→G_m is exactly a weight grading compatible with the fixed model filtration and splitting W on cohomology.
hypotheses: M has finite-dimensional cohomology and a chosen admissible filtration.
All cohomology constraints are imposed as the inverse limit of finite-dimensional algebraic equations.

sources.match: Filtered automorphisms and a G_m extension encode weight gradings.
Finite minimal-algebra automorphism groups are algebraic, with unipotent kernels in the cohomological comparisons.

proofSteps: Describe a map on each finite generating set by its images in the finite-dimensional same-degree spaces. Impose multiplication, differential and filtration equations; invertibility is the corresponding open determinant condition.
Take finite filtered automorphism groups, not unrestricted Aut(M_n) whose restrictions might fail to preserve earlier stages.
Impose the W and graded-scalar conditions on finite cohomology data and pass to the limit. The kernel is proved prounipotent in the next target, rather than assumed by definition.
acceptance: The section corresponding to a grading sends x_w to λ^w x_w.
The group acting trivially on Gr^W H* can act nontrivially on H* itself by W-lowering terms.

U-conjugacy supplies exactly the identity-on-Gr^W conclusion.

nodes.title: Splitting and conjugacy for the weight extension
nodes.statement: For the filtered minimal-model weight extension, U is prounipotent. If G₂→G_m has a section after a field extension L/K, it is scheme-surjective over K. An extension 1→U→G₂→G_m→1 over a characteristic-zero field with the compatible affine algebraic finite-stage structure used here has an algebraic section over K, and any two sections are U(K)-conjugate. The passage from finite-dimensional unipotent groups to the inverse limit includes a compatible-lifting argument; it is not justified by applying finite-dimensional Levi decomposition independently at every stage.
hypotheses: K characteristic zero; the filtered automorphism tower and finite-stage image systems are as in the preceding target.

sources.match: Uses prounipotence, scheme-surjectivity and conjugate splittings.
Finite-dimensional Levi decomposition and the vanishing of unipotent torsors provide the finite-stage input.

proofSteps: Use the triangular minimal-generator filtration to show that an automorphism acting trivially on Gr^W H* acts unipotently on every relevant finite stage. The kernel is a limit of these unipotent image groups.
Use faithful flatness of L/K to descend scheme-surjectivity of the projection.

Apply characteristic-zero reductivity of G_m and the unipotent torsor result to lift sections and their conjugators successively through finite-stage images. Prove the transition lifting and nonempty inverse-limit assertions. G6 isolates this compatibility proof and the precise supplier extension input.
acceptance: A section is an algebraic G_m morphism, not just an abstract homomorphism of K-points.
The conjugator lies in U(K), so its action is identity on Gr^W H*; no claim about homotopy to identity follows.

nodes.title: Rational weight gradings for complex varieties
nodes.statement: For a connected separated finite-type complex variety X and a Sullivan rational minimal model M_Q of X(C), there is a Z-grading M_Q=⊕_w M_(Q,w) by commutative DG subspaces inducing the Hodge weight filtration on cohomology: W_m H^i(X(C),Q)=⊕_(w≤m)H^i(M_Q)_w. This is the complex-variety rational statement of Weil II 5.3.4, not a theorem stated only for varieties over a finite field. The upper index in the sum is m, the same filtration index on the left.
hypotheses: X connected separated finite type over C; geometric mixed Hodge weight filtration supplied as in EH.5.

sources.match: Frobenius first supplies a Q_l grading; the proalgebraic argument descends a splitting to the rational minimal model.

proofSteps: Choose a good Frobenius and a filtration-preserving lift on M_Q⊗Q_l; apply the Weil-weight construction and EH.5.
This gives a section of the weight extension after Q_l scalar extension. Descend scheme-surjectivity and use the prounipotent splitting theorem over Q.
Read the resulting G_m action as a rational grading and compare cohomology weight pieces.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve, degree-one generators have weight 1 and their product has weight 2.
For G_m,C the degree-one generator has weight 2, so the statement is not purity in cochain degree.

nodes.title: Conjugacy of rational weight gradings
nodes.statement: Any two rational weight gradings of M_Q inducing the geometric Hodge weight filtration on H*(X(C),Q) are conjugate by an automorphism of M_Q inducing identity on Gr^W H*(X(C),Q). Conjugacy means g(M_w)=M′_w for every w. The automorphism is not required to induce identity on H* itself, be homotopic to identity, or respect an arbitrarily preselected finite-type filtration.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of the rational weight-splitting theorem.

sources.match: Filtered uniqueness extends to arbitrary two gradings through the common-filtration lemma.

proofSteps: Use the two G_m actions evaluated at 2 and EH.6 common filtration to obtain a finite-type filtration graded for both.
Encode the actions as two sections of a single weight extension.
Conjugate the sections by U(Q) and translate to the subspace gradings. G5 and G6 must be discharged for this unrestricted assertion.
acceptance: Identity on Gr^W is the exact proven condition on the conjugator.
The stronger homotopic-to-identity assertion about filtrations in 5.3.10 is not substituted for this theorem.

nodes.title: Weight gradings over arbitrary algebraically closed fields
nodes.statement: Let X be a connected separated finite-type variety over any algebraically closed field k, with l invertible in k. A Sullivan minimal Q_l-model M of A_l(X) admits integer weight gradings inducing on H*(M)=H*_(ét)(X,Q_l) a splitting of the cohomological weight filtration obtained from suitable Frobenius spreads. Over a finite field of definition geometric Frobenius directly supplies the grading through a stable minimal representative. For general k the comparison uses spreads and common refinements. This theorem asserts existence of a grading over Q_l; it does not assert a rational Q-model of X or a functorial choice of splitting.
hypotheses: X connected, separated finite type; k algebraically closed; l≠char(k).

sources.match: The Frobenius construction yields model gradings splitting cohomological weights for arbitrary algebraically closed base fields.

proofSteps: Descend X to a finitely generated field and spread the cohomological weight comparison of EH.5; verify independence of the cohomological filtration using G4.
Choose a suitable Frobenius and lift it to a stable minimal-model representative.
Apply the Galois-invariant Weil weight homomorphism and its field descent. No descent from Q_l to Q is used in this case.
acceptance: For P¹ minus three rational points over F_q, the geometric H¹ has two weight-2 generators.
The source’s rational complex theorem is distinct from this Q_l existence statement.

nodes.title: Formality of proper smooth varieties
nodes.statement: For a connected proper smooth variety X over an algebraically closed field k with l invertible in k, a Sullivan minimal model M of A_l(X) admits a commutative DG quasi-isomorphism M→(H*_(ét)(X,Q_l),d=0). Thus the same M is a minimal model of the zero-differential cohomology algebra. In a weight grading with M_w^n=0 for w<n and pure weight n on H^n, the map in degree n projects to M_n^n and then takes its cohomology class, killing weights w>n. This is a multiplicative chain map and a cohomology isomorphism.
hypotheses: Proper AND smooth; connected; l invertible; the model has finite cohomology in every degree.

sources.match: Purity and the model weight lower bound give the explicit diagonal quasi-isomorphism.

sources.locator: §6, Main Theorem and first proof, pp. 270–271
sources.match: The classical Kähler formality result is the rational comparison case, not a replacement for the l-adic argument.

proofSteps: Use DWP.7 purity for proper smooth X, including nonprojective X; the smooth-projective result alone is insufficient.
The weight-n part of M^n consists of cycles since d lands in M_n^(n+1)=0.

For the chain-map condition, the image of a differential is a boundary and hence has zero cohomology class even when its weight equals the target degree. The bound and multiplicativity give compatibility with products.
Purity makes the induced map on cohomology an isomorphism. Import the generic formality predicate and its Massey consequences from DGAInfinity.
acceptance: A proper smooth genus≥1 curve is formal; for an elliptic curve the explicit model is Λ(a₁,b₁), d=0.
A merely smooth open variety does not satisfy the purity hypothesis; its weight bounds alone do not justify the diagonal projection theorem.

nodes.title: The Lie tower dual to a 1-minimal model
nodes.statement: For a connected commutative DG K-algebra A with finite-dimensional H¹ and H², construct a 1-minimal map M^(1)→A as an increasing union of finite degree-one Hirsch extensions, giving an H¹ isomorphism and an H² injection. If V_n is the finite-dimensional generator space of a finite stage, transpose d:V_n→Λ²V_n to define the bracket on V_n∨; d²=0 gives Jacobi. These finite nilpotent Lie algebras and their surjective transition maps form a pronilpotent tower. A compatible integer grading on M^(1) dualizes with opposite signs on the Lie tower.
hypotheses: K characteristic zero; H⁰(A)=K; H¹,H² finite-dimensional.
The tower is indexed by finite 1-minimal Hirsch stages; it is not obtained by dualizing an arbitrary infinite vector space without a topology.

sources.match: The degree-one minimal model yields the Malcev Lie tower and the generators-and-relations calculation.
Uses the H¹-isomorphism/H²-injection comparison to control normal-variety relation weights.

proofSteps: Adjoin H¹ generators, then degree-one generators killing the H² kernel, with finite choices at each step.
Use the existing Lie algebra carrier and transpose the quadratic differential at each finite stage.
Compare this tower with the supplier’s unipotent fundamental group; the comparison is a separate target, not part of the definition.
acceptance: The sign reversal turns cohomological weights 1,2 into Lie generator weights −1,−2.
The full minimal model and 1-minimal model need not have the same higher cohomology.

nodes.title: Comparison with the unipotent étale fundamental group
nodes.statement: For a geometrically pointed connected normal variety (X,x) over an algebraically closed field with l invertible, the pronilpotent Lie tower from the 1-minimal model of A_l(X) identifies with the Lie algebras of the finite-dimensional unipotent Q_l-quotients of the continuous étale fundamental-group representation category. Here the geometric group is the unipotent Tannakian fundamental group supplied by NC.2; the maximal profinite étale fundamental group is not identified with its unipotent completion. Pointed maps give the comparison, and forgetting the basepoint gives the usual ambiguity by inner automorphisms.
hypotheses: X normal, separated finite type and connected; geometric basepoint x; l invertible.

sources.match: The l-adic analogue concerns unipotent Lie quotients of π₁.
Explains the unipotent quotient presentation in terms of degree-one cohomology and degree-two relations.
The topological comparison identifies the degree-one minimal model with the rational nilpotent completion; the étale comparison needs its own argument.

proofSteps: Compare the algebraic finite-stage extension category of the degree-one minimal model with successive extensions of the trivial continuous Q_l étale local system. No flat-connection realization on a singular or positive-characteristic variety is assumed.
At each finite unipotence depth match extension H¹ and obstruction H² through the étale cohomology comparison.

Check basepoint fiber functors, bracket and transition maps. G7 and the NC.2 extension request identify this comparison for general normal varieties rather than assuming a theorem for smooth curves suffices.
acceptance: Depth one is dual H¹_(ét)(X,Q_l).
A finite group with trivial rational unipotent completion can have nontrivial finite étale covers; the comparison cannot identify the full profinite group.

nodes.title: Weight-bounded presentations for normal varieties
nodes.statement: Let X be a connected normal separated finite-type variety over an algebraically closed field k, with geometric basepoint x and l invertible in k. The Lie algebra u_l(X,x) of its unipotent étale fundamental group is isomorphic to the lower-central completion of a graded Lie algebra L(V)/(R), where V≃H¹_(ét)(X,Q_l)∨ has weights −1 and −2, L(V) is the free graded Lie algebra, and the homogeneous ideal is generated by a finite-dimensional relation space R supported in weights −2,−3,−4. The choices of generators and presentation are noncanonical. Its finite unipotent quotients are obtained by the compatible nilpotent/lower-central truncations; one must also include the nilpotence cutoff when presenting a finite quotient.
hypotheses: X connected normal separated finite type; k algebraically closed; l≠char(k).
Use the weight filtration on cohomology and the 1-minimal étale comparison of EH.8.

sources.match: Announces the normal-variety l-adic analogue of Morgan.
States the normal-variety presentation: two generator weights and three relation weights.
The smooth-complex version explains the 1-minimal proof; its Hodge bidegrees are not imposed on singular normal X.

sources.locator: p. 185, revised Theorem 9.2 and final paragraph
sources.match: Corrects functoriality claims about indecomposables; the presentation result 9.4 is retained.

proofSteps: Normality gives H¹ weights 1 and 2, so dual generators have weights −1 and −2.
The 1-minimal H² injection makes the relation space a quotient of H²(X,Q_l)∨. General cohomological weights put it in [−4,0].
Relations are brackets, hence have weight≤−2. Intersecting the two bounds leaves exactly −2,−3,−4.

Each of these weight pieces in the free Lie algebra on finite-dimensional negative-weight V is finite-dimensional; choose a finite homogeneous relation space and complete for the lower central series.
acceptance: For P¹ minus three points V has two weight −2 generators and R=0: all finite nilpotent free quotients occur.
For a proper smooth elliptic curve V has two weight −1 generators and the relation [a,b]=0 of weight −2, giving an abelian Lie algebra.
A proper nodal rational curve is not normal and has H¹ of weight 0; it is excluded from the negative-generator-weight statement.

gaps.title: Integral coefficient resolution and finite-width proof
gaps.detail: Weil II 5.1.9(b), pp. 236–237, gives a proof outline but refers to Quillen décalage and Miller, De Rham cohomology with arbitrary coefficients (Topology 17 (1978), 193–203), for the integral theorem.
